#1714. Liverpool Confidential: Billionaires' investment set to beat deadline, new deal for Trey Nyoni, the academy kids who shone in Istanbul and Mor Talla Ndiaye's visa issues

Published: 12:00 EST, 5 November 2026 | Updated: 12:04 EST, 5 November 2026

The deal for a group of billionaires to buy a minority stake in Liverpool remains on track to pass a deadline set by the new independent football regulator.

The consortium led by Amit Bhatia, known as 1892 Holdings, agreed to purchase a 38 per cent stake in Fenway Sports Group’s controlling interest in the club earlier this season. And despite some anxieties externally and in the fanbase about a lack of updates, I have been told this week that everything is moving in the right direction.

Sources close to Bhatia and his consortium insist the process takes time but there are no hitches and it is still expected to beat the deadline. It is understood the date in question is in December and in accordance with the new regulator, who must take within 90 days to issue a final suitability determination for prospective new owners or senior executives.

Indeed, this week brought the news that FSG are in exploratory talks to buy a significant stake in Formula One team Cadillac. Both FSG and Cadillac were contacted for comment around that story – and insisted it is an ongoing process.

One source pointed to the fact that FSG clearly expect to have some ‘spare pennies lying around’ – hinting the Liverpool investment will go through.

Senior FSG staff have constantly stressed that selling 38 per cent of the club does not mean they are losing interest and that they are as committed as ever, though the potential for the buy-in to become a full-scale takeover at some point in the future remains.

Bhatia is backed by his billionaire father-in-law Lakshmi Mittal, plus Jeff Bezos and Eduardo Saverin.

Amit Bhatia (second left) is heading up a consortium to buy a stake in Liverpool from John Henry (second right) and his Fenway Sports Group

Liverpool supporters hope the deal will transform the club's fortunes on the pitch

Jeremie Frimpong has had rotten luck with injuries since he joined Liverpool – and Andoni Iraola ruled him out for more than a month with a problem he suffered at Brentford on October 17.

I understand the Dutch international is now all-but fit and could play this weekend if needed – however, given his high number of injuries, a decision has been made to delay his return.

Liverpool were recently punished for bringing back Dominik Szoboszlai too quickly as the Hungarian pulled up shortly after his first start upon his return, which set him back a fortnight.

Frimpong missed only seven Bayer Leverkusen games through injury in four years at the club according to Transfermarkt, but has already sat out nearly 30 Liverpool matches. Most of those absences have been hamstring related, so Frimpong is not being rushed back and will be given the international break to continue working on his recovery.

Jeremie Frimpong has had rotten luck with injuries since he joined Liverpool and went down again against Brentford last month. However, the Dutch international is now close to a return

Trey Nyoni has been offered a bumper new contract to reward him for his fine progress.

The 19-year-old, who scored his first Liverpool goal in the defeat in Istanbul against Fenerbahce on Wednesday night, has had a stellar rise since Iraola took over at Liverpool.

Nyoni, signed from Leicester City in 2023, was in many matchday squads and featured sparingly last season but has come of age this campaign and has already doubled his first-team minutes – with three quarters of the season still to play.

Nottingham Forest made a £30million bid in the summer but Iraola identified him as a key asset and he will be rewarded handsomely for his progress.

Trey Nyoni scored his first Liverpool goal on Wednesday night in the Champions League loss against Fenerbahce

Your question answered: What's the January priority?

One topic fans have asked me about this week is which position is a priority in the January and summer transfer windows.

The first area to mention is midfield. I have reported in the past how Chelsea are currently ahead of Liverpool in the race for Bournemouth's Alex Scott, so let’s keep an eye on that – and the situation of Lamine Camara of Monaco. But I think the priority has to be a left-back.

Are Milos Kerkez and Kostas Tsimikas good enough? Neither have performed at the required level so far this season and bringing Tsimikas back from a loan at Roma – where he barely played – felt like a bit of a cop-out. It has to be a priority position in the next 12 months.

Liverpool flew straight home from Istanbul after the loss to Fenerbahce and did not land on Merseyside until past 2am. It is a departure from last season, when Arne Slot would often have his squad stay for two nights on European away days.

Players are said to be big fans of the extra night at home with most preferring to sleep in their own beds.

Iraola did not hold a post-match team talk after Fenerbahce but will debrief the squad when back in training, having branded the defeat ‘cheap’ and ‘messy’.

Another UEFA Youth League game, another hat-trick for Will Wright.

I was in place on the outskirts of Istanbul on Wednesday afternoon to watch the 18-year-old bag his second treble in four European matches this term, making it 13 goals for the season in all competitions.

Wright had a heated exchange with Josh Sonni-Lambie over who would take a penalty but the pair have smoothed things over now after Wright took it and scored. The striker’s assist for Finn Inglethorpe was also a notable moment that showed he is a team player and not a greedy No9.

Liverpool's Will Wright scored another hat-trick in the UEFA Youth League on Wednesday, against Fenerbahce Under 19s

I was also impressed by right back Oliver O’Connor, who looks like a real athlete. He aced every physical pre-season test for the academy and is versatile, with a quality delivery into the penalty area.

The Scouser joined the club aged six and has been a midfielder for most of his career. Boss Rob Page does not necessarily see him as a right back long-term but he caught the eye up and down that flank.

Those who did watch the academy game – and the first-team later on – would have been wondering where defender Mor Talla Ndiaye was. He is a mainstay in the Youth League XI and has been on the seniors’ bench several times.

It is believed the Senegalese defender had a visa issue and could not feature in the game in Turkey, though next month’s away match in Bruges is not expected to pose the same problem.

Liverpool's Mor Talla Ndiaye (centre) was nowhere to be seen in Istanbul due to visa issues

Also in academy news, young midfielder Michael Laffey has signed with the OmniSports agency who represent the likes of Wright and Crystal Palace midfielder Adam Wharton. Under 21s captain Laffey, whose dad owns the Glenbuck pub in Anfield, made the first-team bench a fortnight ago.

Liverpool supporters have drawn the short straw and will pay more than any of their English counterparts for a pint while following their team in Europe this season.

That’s according to data from LiveScore, who have worked out that Reds will pay an average of £4.91 per pint on their travels.

Still, £4.91 for a pint? Better than most places at home. You might need one after watching Liverpool’s defending this week!

#1713. Plymouth Argyle vs Swindon Town - prediction, team news, lineups

By Freddie Cotton | 08 Nov 2026 23:18

Plymouth Argyle welcome Swindon Town to Home Park on Tuesday evening for their third and final EFL Trophy group stage fixture.

In their previous competition outing, the Pilgrims prevailed on penalties after drawing against Newport County at Rodney Parade, while the Robins fell to a 2-0 defeat to the same opposition at the County Ground.

Having been eliminated from the tournament at the quarterfinal stage in the 2025-26 campaign, falling to a late 2-1 loss against eventual winners Luton Town, Plymouth will be determined to go one better this season and finish the group stage on a high.

After starting their campaign in emphatic fashion by thumping Crystal Palace U21s 5-1, the Pilgrims could only manage a draw away to Newport, but having claimed victory in the resulting penalty shootout, Tuesday’s hosts picked up two points from their trip to Wales and as a result, confirmed their spot in the knockout stages.

Plymouth have impressed outside of the EFL Trophy too, as after 14 matches Tom Cleverley’s men sit fifth in League One, just three points off the automatic promotion places, while also booking their place in the FA Cup second-round on Saturday afternoon with a thumping 4-0 victory over Southern League Premier Central side Alvechurch at Home Park.

While they only need a draw to rise to the summit of Group 13 on Tuesday evening, the Pilgrims should by no means be underestimating League Two Swindon Town, with the Robins claiming victory in three of their previous four visits to South West Devon.

Following their expulsion from the competition in the 2025-26 campaign, having fielded two ineligible players in their round-of-16 tie with Luton at Kenilworth Road, Swindon will be left extremely disappointed with their efforts in the EFL Trophy this season too.

Despite taking the lead, Ian Holloway’s men began their campaign with a 2-1 home defeat against Crystal Palace U21s and, having also lost to Newport at the County Ground just a week later, the Robins can no longer progress to the knockout phase, meaning Tuesday’s match is purely a matter of pride for the visitors.

Unlike their opponents, Swindon are struggling for form elsewhere too, having won just two of their previous nine League Two fixtures to leave them languishing in mid-table, while their FA Cup campaign has already come to an end following a 2-1 first-round defeat to third tier side Milton Keynes Dons.

However, while they find themselves a division below Tuesday’s hosts, the Robins have a particularly good recent record when facing Plymouth, winning two of their previous three matches against the Pilgrims, including an impressive 3-1 win when the sides met at Home Park in October 2021.

Plymouth will be without both Matthew Sorinola and Caleb Watts for Tuesday’s clash as the pair continue their recovery from knee and groin injuries respectively, while Julio Pleguezuelo is a doubt after suffering a calf problem in training last week.

Having been rested against Alvechurch as a precaution, Scottish defender Jack MacKenzie is likely to return to the fold for the Pilgrims this week and so too is Owen Oseni, who featured on the bench on Saturday following a month's absence with an ankle issue.

After missing the entirety of the start of the season, Cleverley also welcomed back Ghanaian midfielder Michael Baidoo in the FA Cup on the weekend and the 27-year-old capped his return with a goal.

Following only his second ever international call up, Swindon will be without Moldovan defender Stephan Negru on Tuesday evening, while Samuel Inwood is also unavailable across the backline with a serious hamstring injury.

Having undergone knee surgery in September, Ben Middlemas continues to be sidelined for the Robins, who will also be missing Ollie Clarke after the 34-year-old sustained a hamstring issue against Barnet a fortnight ago.

Both Paul Glatzel and Anthony Munda remain out for Holloway’s side too with knee problems and the visitor’s injury list is rounded off with Fletcher Holman, who is expected to be back in the new year from a severe hamstring tear.

On a more positive note for Swindon, 20-year-old midfielder Jaylan Pearman returned to the squad against MK Dons from an illness and will be looking to get some more minutes under his belt this week.

Plymouth Argyle possible starting lineup:

Storer; Edwards, Ross, MacKenzie, Rendle; Amaechi, Campbell, Roberts, Pepple; Oseni, Ibrahim

Ward; Debayo, Ball, Kirkman; Griffiths-Brown, Nichols, Butterworth, Clark; Hoare, Hackford, Pearman

Boasting a positive recent record against Plymouth, Swindon will be determined to end their disappointing EFL Trophy campaign on a high this week, while maintaining their impressive streak against the Pilgrims.

However, despite expecting both sides to make changes to their line-ups on Tuesday, we are backing Cleverley’s men to claim all three points and secure top spot in Group 13.

#1712. Report: Liverpool to beat Barcelona to £75m Virgil van Dijk replacement

Virgil van Dijk is undoubtedly one of the best defenders in history, but his time at Anfield cannot last forever.

The legendary Liverpool captain is into the final 12 months of his deal, and as things stand will be leaving Merseyside for free in the summer.

At 35-years-old, the Dutchman has played every minute of the Reds' Premier League campaign so far, in what could be his final season at Anfield.

Julian Ward and Liverpool's recruitment team have already begun planning for a potential departure, and one star is now reportedly being lined up for a massive £75 million move.

Barcelona to battle Liverpool for Premier League defenderSeveral of Europe's top defenders have been identified as potential replacements for Liverpool's skipper, but one move now gaining traction is for Chelsea's Levi Colwill. The 23-year-old has started all but one of the Blues' Premier League games this season, captaining his side on three occasions. Now, the Reds are lining up a move that could cost as much as £75 million to bring the five-capped England international to Merseyside.

Several of Europe's top defenders have been identified as potential replacements for Liverpool's skipper, but one move now gaining traction is for Chelsea's Levi Colwill.

The 23-year-old has started all but one of the Blues' Premier League games this season, captaining his side on three occasions.

Now, the Reds are lining up a move that could cost as much as £75 million to bring the five-capped England international to Merseyside.

That's according to a report from Caught Offside, which claims that Liverpool hold a strong interest in the defender and will try and convince him to consider a new challenge.

The report states that Chelsea want to keep Colwill at Stamford Bridge but that they could consider a bid of between £65-75 million.

Liverpool aren't the only team interested in the 23-year-old however, with La Liga leaders Barcelona also monitoring the situation.

Chelsea would likely be more willing to deal with a team in another league rather than selling one of their best players to a direct rival, but if the Reds can make an attractive enough offer then they may be able to land their man.

Colwill has been on the radar at Anfield for some time, and Liverpool could finally act on their long-term interest to replace Van Dijk, should the Dutchman leave in the summer.

#1711. Man United news: New manager 'favourite' other than Eddie Howe and Julian Nagelsmann amid Michael Carrick sack pressure

By Lewis Nolan | 08 Nov 2026 23:47

Mauricio Pochettino has joined the likes of Eddie Howe and Julian Nagelsmann as favourites to replace Manchester United boss Michael Carrick.

The Red Devils earned a point in their final Premier League game before the start of the international break, with the club drawing 4-4 with Aston Villa on Sunday.

Carrick's side came back from 2-0 and 4-2 deficits to avoid defeat, though the result left the team in 18th place, and their placement has fuelled calls for a change in the dugout.

A number of managers have been linked with Old Trafford, including former Newcastle boss Howe and former Bayern Munich head coach Nagelsmann.

However, the Evening Standard have claimed that current USA national team coach Pochettino has emerged as a leading contender should Carrick lose his job.

Most United supporters will remember Pochettino from his time at Tottenham Hotspur, with the 54-year-old spending five years at the club between 2014 and 2019.

While he failed to win a trophy in London, the Argentine managed to reach the 2014-15 EFL Cup final, as well as the 2018-19 Champions League final, while he guided the club to two third-placed finishes, one second-placed finish and one fourth-placed finish.

It should be noted that Pochettino was dealing with a restricted transfer budget for much of his time at Spurs, yet he created one of the most exciting teams in the division, getting the most out of stars like Harry Kane, Dele Alli, Christian Eriksen and Son Heung-min.

Failed spells at Paris Saint-Germain and Chelsea following his exit from Tottenham in 2019 should not overshadow his qualities as a coach, and if he can get the Red Devils to play as energetically as his Spurs side did, then United will be a threat against most opponents.

Even though there may be some concerns about Pochettino's ability to get the club over the line in the biggest moments, United are not in a position to turn down someone with the track record of the Argentine.

No other team have won fewer games in the Premier League this season than United (one), and the club are only one point above last-placed Crystal Palace.

The Red Devils are set for a difficult test against Liverpool at Anfield after the international break, and heading into that game without fundamental changes could be disastrous.

Many fans are fond of Carrick for his contributions as a player at Old Trafford, and perhaps now would be the best time to dismiss him with the chance to walk away after a spirited comeback rather than a potentially devastating result against the Merseysiders.

#1709. Opinion: Liverpool handed major transfer boost in chase for £45m sensation

Liverpool were probably expecting their squad to be completed by now.

They've spent over £600 million on new players across the last couple of seasons and, if we're being honest, things still aren't great.

Multiple areas of of Andoni Iraola's squad have failed to meet the standards expected of them and have forced fans to question whether some of the players that their team have signed were even worth buying in the first place.

This thought process has led to different questions being asked about their first-team squad and has caused many players to be linked with a move.

And now, the Anfield outfit seem to have just been handed a major boost in their pursuit for one of their main targets.

Barcelona want to sign Levi Colwill which could open the door for a Ronald Araujo transfer

Ronald Araujo has arguably been one of Liverpool's best signings this season.

The Uruguayan was brought in on a season-long loan with the Reds having an option to buy worth €55 million (£45.9 million).

This may not seem like all that much money with how good the centre-back has been but, since he'll be 28 years old by the time Liverpool can activate their option to buy, it's unclear whether he'll be worth them signing or not.

Obviously, things such as his injury history also need to be taken into consideration.

But, luckily for Liverpool, a fresh update from Caught Offside has shared that Barcelona now want to sign Levi Colwill from Chelsea.

"Barcelona view Colwill as a top target after studying his performances and stats in great detail, there have been internal discussions about putting a bid together, possibly as early as this January," they wrote.

Levi Colwill could be Barcelona's replacement for Ronald Araujo

With how happy Araujo seems to be at Liverpool and how happy the Reds' fanbase seems to be with the Uruguayan, a permanent deal for him makes sense.

His ability to play as a right-back or a centre-back is massive with both of those areas major problems for Liverpool at the moment.

In fact, their whole defence could do with a re-jig.

Barca are likely to stick to their price of €55 million for Araujo but, if they manage to get a deal over the line for Colwill before then, they could become a little more lenient.

Araujo's experience is unmatched compared to some of the other players that Liverpool have been linked with.

But, only time will tell whether the Reds feel like a move for the 27-year-old is worth it.

#1708. Ex-Man United star Clayton Blackmore is forced to apologise for encouraging Mason Greenwood to 'come home to us' after winger beat Liverpool with Fenerbahce

By BEN WILLCOCKS, ASSISTANT SPORTS EDITOR

Published: 13:06 EST, 5 November 2026 | Updated: 13:28 EST, 5 November 2026

Former Manchester United footballer Clayton Blackmore has apologised after being criticised on social media for asking Mason Greenwood to 'come home' to Old Trafford.

Greenwood, 25, played a pivotal role for Fenerbahce during their 3-2 victory over Manchester United's archrivals Liverpool in the Champions League on Wednesday, scoring the Turkish giants' first-half equaliser.

The English forward broke through the ranks as a youngster at Manchester United and looked destined to become a key long-term player, but his career spiralled after he was arrested and charged in 2022 with suspected attempted rape, controlling and coercive behaviour and assault causing actual bodily harm.

Although those charges were subsequently dropped by the Crown Prosecution Service in February 2023, United decided Greenwood could not continue to ply his trade at Old Trafford after undertaking an internal six-month investigation.

Since his exit, which came after disgruntled Manchester United supporters groups heaped pressure on the club to cut ties with the forward, Greenwood has represented Spanish club Getafe on loan, French giants Marseille and Turkish side Fenerbahce, who he joined this summer for a reported €39million (£33.27million).

Blackmore, who played for Manchester United between 1982 and 1994, was met with backlash on Thursday after he heaped praise on Greenwood for his role in Fenerbahce's 3-2 win over Liverpool.

Mason Greenwood (centre) celebrates after scoring in Fenerbahce's 3-2 win over Liverpool

Former Man United star Clayton Blackmore pleaded for Grenwood to 'come home to us'

The 62-year-old Welshman apologised after his post was met with a furious backlash online

Greenwood's Manchester United career ended after he was charged with attempted rape, controlling and coercive behaviour and assault causing actual bodily harm in 2022

'Well done Mason Greenwood beating Liverpool. Come home to us please,' the Welshman, 62, posted on X.

Two hours later, after receiving a slew of disparaging comments on the platform, he said: 'Sorry I've offended anyone but I heard he had been cleared of any wrongdoing I apologise to everyone I've upset with my comments like I said I thought he had been cleared of everything and he’s had a baby with his girlfriend. Big sorry.'

Blackmore had previously come under fire for expressing his sadness that both Greenwood and Angel Gomes, another former English prodigy who was sold to Lille by Manchester United in 2020, no longer play for the club.

When the duo were both playing at Marseille last season, Blackmore said on X: 'Good to see Angel Gomez and Mason Greenwood score Marseille in first 26 mins. Sad they're not still at United.'

After landing himself in hot water with the post, he clarified to those commenting: 'Sorry I understand what you're saying but sometimes everything you hear is not always the truth why did his girlfriend stay with him I'm just looking at the football side.'

He later doubled down and wrote: 'Sorry didn't see or hear any of that I will do my home work next time just looking at it from the football side sorry if I've offended anyone especially his girlfriend and her family.'

While there was noisy resistance to Greenwood joining Marseille in the summer of 2025, he found no such opposition in Turkey, where one prominent journalist claimed 95 per cent of the population would not know or care about his past.

He didn't face any questions about the dropped charges or his public image in his first press conference and outside of brief post-match comments, has not conducted any interviews of note.

Greenwood has been hiding from the limelight a record signing would usually bask in, especially in the football-crazed city of Istanbul.

He found a home in a district called Sarıyer, a favourite among footballers, who largely live in gated communities.

Greenwood is said to count team-mates N'Golo Kante and Marco Asensio as neighbours and was seen in a rare online post after securing his new home, posing with the all-female team of estate agents who helped him with the purchase.

The former United starlet completed his move to Turkish giants Fenerbahce in the summer

Blackmore had previously come under fire for expressing his sadness at Greenwood leaving

Since the big-money move, Greenwood has only posted a handful of times on his Instagram profile, all of which were generic action shots after matches.

His latest offering came after Fenerbahce's stunning win over Liverpool, as he posted a gallery of photographs celebrating in the club's yellow and black jersey.

His partner, Harriet, 26, is also selective with how much she shares from their new life.

She only has four posts in total, with around 20 photos in each 'round-up', offering a glimpse into the high-life, though Greenwood himself only appears twice.

One of the images is of him looking exhausted in hospital at the birth of their second daughter in 2023 and another shows him holding hands with their eldest, Summer, who is three.

#1707. Crawley Town vs Brentford U21 - prediction, team news, lineups

By Anthony Nolan | 09 Nov 2026 00:18, Last updated: 09 Nov 2026 05:23

A spot in the EFL Trophy's round of 32 is up for grabs at Broadfield Stadium, when Crawley Town host Brentford U21 for their final showdown in Southern Group H on Tuesday.

The Red Devils are hoping to bounce back after a humiliating FA Cup exit, while the Bees are searching for their third win in four games.

Crawley sacked Colin Kazim-Richards last month, leaving former Leeds United and Sheffield United manager Kevin Blackwell in interim charge until a replacement can be appointed.

The 67-year-old has collected four points from his two league matches in the dugout, drawing 1-1 with Tranmere Rovers before beating Oldham Athletic 1-0 on October 31.

That latest success has seen the Red Devils build up a tally of nine points in League Two, though they remain at the bottom of the table, three points short of 22nd-placed Rotherham United having played two games fewer.

The only negative from Blackwell's tenure to date was the 2-0 FA Cup elimination at the hands of Southern Premier Division South club Wimborne Town on Sunday.

In the EFL Trophy, Crawley sit second in Southern Group H, level on points with their opponents but armed with the knowledge that a draw would likely be enough to see them through to the round of 32, owing to their six-superior goal-difference.

Blackwell's side will be desperate to avoid what would be another demoralising cup exit after seemingly turning a corner in League Two, and they will be buoyed by playing on home turf, where the hosts beat Bromley 4-0 in the EFL Trophy on October 6.

Meanwhile, Sam Saunders's Brentford U21 arrive in commendable form and ready for the challenge of facing senior professionals once again, having won two of their last three outings.

The Bees beat Bournemouth U21 4-3 in a dramatic Premier League 2 showdown on October 26, and built on that triumph with a 2-1 victory over Wycombe Wanderers U21 in the Premier League Cup.

However, Saunders's youngsters were downed 2-0 by Wolverhampton Wanderers U21 on Friday, failing to find the back of the net for the first time in eight games.

That defeat has left Brentford U21 14th in the Premier League 2 table with nine points from seven matches, winning three and losing four of those fixtures, and notably both scoring and conceding 15 goals.

The Bees were hammered 7-1 by group leaders MK Dons last time out in the EFL Trophy, and everyone involved in the club's youth setup will be keen to prevent a second consecutive thrashing in the competition.

Crawley could name a similar lineup to the one that faced Wimborne in the FA Cup, with Danilo Orsi-Dadomo up top, supported by a trio consisting of Stephen Duke-McKenna, Kai Jennings and Dylan Morgan.

Charlie Barker could start at the base of midfield, operating alongside Jude Arthurs just in front of centre-backs Priestley Farquharson and Johnny Russell, with Akinwale Odimayo having undergone surgery on a major injury after being stretchered off in the 2-2 draw against Chesterfield last month.

As for Brentford U21, they will be without senior attacker Fabio Carvalho - who featured in the 1-0 win over Bromley - due to a knock, while 19-year-old striker Kaye Furo is recovering from surgery on a foot injury.

In their absence, Isaac Holland should lead the line, and is likely to be supplied by Ollie Shield, Jacob Hanson and Gustavo Nunes.

Elsewhere, midfielder Antoni Milambo is sidelined after suffering a minor setback following a brief return from his cruciate ligament injury, so Riley Owen and Kiefer Gorman look set to start in the Bees' double pivot.

Mannone; Gordon, Farquharson, Russell, Richards; Barker, Arthurs; Duke-McKenna, Jennings, Morgan; Orsi-Dadomo

Rose; Wheeler-Henry, Avenell, Grey, Picotto; Gorman, Owen; Shield, Hanson, Gustavo Nunes; Holland

Crawley will be optimistic given they are facing a youth side, but fans will be wary after seeing their team stunned by a Southern Premier Division South club in the FA Cup.

Brentford U21 may be fearful after receiving a thrashing last time out in the EFL Trophy, but if the youngsters can settle their nerves, then a narrow win could be on the cards.

#1706. Mykhailo Mudryk returns as Chelsea slip to Juventus defeat

Mykhailo Mudryk made his first Chelsea appearance since November 2024 as Xabi Alonso’s team succumbed to their second pre-season defeat.

Mudryk replaced Nicolas Jackson in the 82nd minute against Juventus, marking his return to competitive football after a long doping ban that was resolved this week thanks to changes in Wada regulations.

There were a couple of crosses delivered from the left flank by the Ukrainian winger, who could yet leave Chelsea on loan or on a permanent basis before the close of the transfer window.

Juventus were the victors though, thanks to a sumptuous 68th-minute goal by Kosovo winger Edon Zhegrova.

Alonso had 21 players on his bench, and made 12 second-half substitutions.

Levi Colwill and Cole Palmer featured in the defeat by 10-man Spurs on Saturday, but sat this game out as they continue to build fitness. Danny Welbeck did start though, reunited with former Brighton team-mate Joao Pedro up top.

Chelsea scored just one goal against Spurs and Juventus, but the thrust provided by right-back Marco Palestra in tandem with first Geovany Quenda and then Estevao was a bright spot for Alonso.

Chelsea continue their pre-season against AC Milan on Saturday, before they host Real Sociedad at Stamford Bridge on August 15.

They begin their Premier League campaign at Fulham in the Monday night slot on the opening weekend.

Even Chelsea’s in-house streaming had given up the ghost by the end. Consecutive pre-season defeats for Chelsea, but worth remembering that Colwill and Palmer sat out this fitness exercise and Enzo Fernandez is still to return. Palestra’s performances a real positive but the team is still finding its way.

Juventus win a corner late on, but Yildiz’s delivery is too close to Penders. Just two minutes for Chelsea to find an equaliser.

Mudryk does well to dig out a cross from the left but the goalkeeper Perin gathers. There will be four minutes of added time to play.

Chelsea not really threatening an equaliser as the game meanders towards a conclusion. Should they score a goal, we will have a penalty shoot-out.

Estevao looked for Mudryk with a reverse pass between full-back and centre-back but there was too much weight on the ball.

Estevao’s free-kick is saved but the bigger news for Chelsea fans is that Mykhailo Mudryk has been introduced from the bench, replacing Nicolas Jackson for the closing stages.

Lavia and Liam Delap involved in some handbags with the Juventus players, Bremer the centre-back in the thick of things too and has been shown a yellow card. Chelsea have a free-kick, Estevao over it from 35 yards out.

Just the one goal scored for Chelsea against top level opponents in pre-season, but I doubt Alonso will be panicking just yet. Chelsea play Milan this weekend before hosting Real Sociedad on August 15th in their final pre season friendly.

Juventus goalkeeper Perin sells Nicolas Jackson a dummy so he can pick a pass into midfield. The Italian side controlling the game quite well since the goal, against a weaker Chelsea team.

Chelsea’s younger players will have to dig them out of trouble in the last 20 minutes. There has not been much in the game, Chelsea have shaded it in general play without quite creating enough.

The Kosovan winger with a first-time, left-footed hit from almost 25 yards, curled into the top corner. Nothing Penders could do about it.

More changes from Chelsea: Anselmino, Acheampong, Satpaev, Assugo and Delap the players on, replacing Hato, Palestra, Gittens, Caicedo and Pedro. Alonso finishing the team with his younger players on the pitch.

Jonathan David slides a pass across the Chelsea six-yard box when there was a chance to shoot, but the flag was up for offside in any case.

Penders does well to palm away an inswinging cross from Zhegrova, before Estevao picks out the run of Palestra on the break with a brilliant forward pass. Chelsea corner, cleared. Now Caicedo has been booked for a cynical challenge to stop a break, much like Douglas Luiz.

Nicolas Jackson hacked down by Douglas Luiz after he turned on halfway with three or four Chelsea runners in support. Painful one for Jackson, and a yellow card for the former Aston Villa midfielder. Chelsea players not happy with that challenge in a pre-season game.

Chelsea certainly have the upper hand in the game, quick feet from Joao Pedro to win a free-kick in midfield. If either team is going to score the game’s first goal, you fancy it will be them.

This time Chelsea find Palestra with a ball over the top, but his shot at goal is at a comfortable height for the goalkeeper.

Palestra popping up in a centre-forward position again, but his shot towards goal is not struck cleanly. The right-back at the heart of Chelsea’s attacking again.

Two very different XIs out there for the second half.

Penders replaces Sanchez in goal, Sarr on for Tosin, Estevao on for Quenda and Jackson on for Welbeck.

For Juventus: Bremer, Perin, Zhegrova, Owusu and David are on.

Not much to write/phone/WhatsApp home about, so far. The combination between Quenda and Palestra down Chelsea’s right has been the best feature of their football, am sure we will see Estevao on that flank in the second half among other changes. The bumpy pitch and a hydration break has not helped the spectacle.

There will be four minutes of stoppage time, simply a result of the hydration break.

Far too much space opens up between Chelsea’s defence and midfield, with Meritti turning and carrying the ball forward. Boga tests Sanchez with a strike from the edge of the box. That was probably Juventus’s most threatening attack.

Palestra defends well as the last man up against Milik, Chelsea almost undone by Locatelli’s outside of the foot pass.

Robert Sanchez caught under a cross swung to the back post, very unconvincing goalkeeping, but Juventus could not get their shot away in the box. Nicoll-Jazuli then did well to bring the ball away for Chelsea at the edge of the box.

Chelsea have another corner, and yet again it comes from a right-sided attack. Chelsea are in ascendancy now after a slow start, but it is a very low intensity contest.

Caicedo with a couple of threatening crosses from a centre-right position, but no Chelsea player can connect with them cleanly. Gittens’s dribbling down the left causing problems for Cambiaso, and he was the one attacking Caicedo’s cross at the back post.

Play has now resumed after the drinks break. No changes from either team, those will come at half time. Chelsea have 21 players sitting on their bench, albeit a number of academy players are on tour.

Time for a hydration break, even though the game is being played under a closed roof.

Chelsea’s right side is their most dangerous, by a distance. Quenda does well to slip Palestra in on the overlap, and his low cross into the six-yard box is cleared for a corner. Juventus clear. Boga with a burst through the Chelsea midfield but the Juventus man then gets his pass wrong.

Kelly with a left-to-right switch to Cambiaso, and his cross deflects off the toe of Miretti in the middle and trickles just wide of the far post. Sanchez was scrambling but I think the goalkeeper had it covered.

Chelsea enjoying their most sustained spell of possession in Juventus’s half so far, without quite carving out a clear cut chance. Juventus defending their penalty area with a back five, but they do not have Bonucci, Chiellini and Barzagli back there anymore.

Quenda with a threatening inswinging cross from the right flank, but Welbeck could not quite rise high enough to direct his header towards the far corner. Quenda was keeping the width for Chelsea with Palestra inside the winger in the box. Quenda then slices a shot over from long range.

Welbeck and Caicedo involved in some good combination play, with Nicoll-Jazuli’s outside of the foot pass finding Gittens. Chelsea’s left-winger runs into traffic, but he has been one of the bright spots of the pre-season campaign thus far.

Having watched a couple of Chelsea’s friendlies, there is a lot to like about Palestra at right-back. Tall, long stride, lots of composure on the ball. Will be interesting to see if they can find a way for him and Reece James to start games. Chelsea as a team yet to find much rhythm in the game so far.

Tosin could well find himself down the pecking order this season among Chelsea’s raft of centre-backs, but he makes an important block in the area before Locatelli drags a shot wide from the edge of the box.

Former Bournemouth defender Lloyd Kelly is in the Juventus team. The Italian team are looking to press high in the early minutes whenever Chelsea try to play out from the back. Quenda with an early dart at the Juventus defence but he gets the pass all wrong with Palestra overlapping.

Palestra with a loose first touch but he recovers and defends well. Like in Sydney, this looks another very bumpy pitch, you can see the join marks between the pieces of turf that have been freshly laid. Coming out of these games without any injuries will be a priority for Alonso.

Juventus get the game started in their pale pink away kit.

Juventus XI: Di Gregorio, Kalulu, Gatti, Kelly, Cambiaso, Douglas Luiz, Locatelli, Miretti, Boga, Milik, Celik

Subs: Perrin, Pinsoglio, Nava, Bremmer, Rugani, Koopmeiners, Arthur Melo, Cabal, Owusu, Gil Puche, Oboavwoduo, Licina, Durmisi, Yildiz, Zhegrova, David

Welbeck starts against Juventus, but no Jordan Henderson with the group just yet. As Sam Dean writes here: “Last season, especially, provided evidence that the balance of their squad was not right, and they are now trying to change the internal dynamic by adding more leadership and experience to the team.”

How long will he stay there? Will he play his way back into Alonso’s team, be shipped out on loan or sold for a fee? Sam Dean assesses the options for player and club in this piece. Out of sight, out of mind could well be the most likely outcome for a player who has missed almost two years of football, and looked extremely raw before his ban.

Looks like a back four once again for Alonso, and Danny Welbeck makes his first Chelsea appearance. Pedro will play off Welbeck as a second striker. Geovany Quenda was signed last year from Sporting CP, but joined up with Chelsea this summer. Another wide forward in their collection.

Chelsea XI: Sanchez; Palestra, Fofana, Tosin, Hato; Caicedo, Nicoll-Jazuli; Quenda, Joao Pedro, Gittens; Welbeck

Chelsea subs: Penders, Sharman-Lowe, Curd, Slonina, Acheampong, Subuloye, Sarr, Diakite, Anselmino, Lavia, Essugo, Watson, Walsh, Kellyman, Mudryk, Estevao Willian, Kavuma-McQueen, Neto, Satpayev, Jackson, Delap

The wheels of commerce continue to turn for Chelsea in the transfer market but this afternoon Xabi Alonso’s team continue their preparations for the new season against Juventus in Hong Kong.

They have the chance to recover from the ignominy of losing to 10-man Tottenham Hotspur in Sydney on Saturday, but with 19 days until Chelsea’s Premier League opener against Fulham these matches are still a fitness building exercise. The positive from the Spurs game was Wesley Fofana, Levi Colwill, Cole Palmer completing 80 minutes – three players who endured injury problems last season.

Another new arrival is expected to follow Morgan Rogers, Marco Palesta, Maxence Lacroix, Jordan Henderson and Danny Welbeck to Stamford Bridge, with the club nearing a deal for Rayo Vallecano left-back Pep Chavarria.

It wouldn’t be Chelsea without talk of some eye-catching outgoings, with Spurs reportedly interested in Nicolas Jackson and Enzo Maresca eyeing a reunion with Pedro Neto at Manchester City.

Alonso’s team promise to be flexible in their tactical approach this season, but so far he has set up with a back four rather than the 3-4-2-1 system he used to such great effect at Bayer Leverkusen. That could change as availability increases closer to the start of the season, but Palestra’s bursts forward from right-back in tandem with Estevao have caught the eye.

Juventus finished sixth in Serie A last season under Luciano Spalletti, the former Roma and Napoli coach who usually guarantees expansive and attractive football. Turkey left-winger Kenan Yildiz was their top goalscorer last season, and it looks like they will make it through the summer without the left-winger being picked off by one of the Premier League’s elite. Yildiz scored 11 goals in all competitions, and Dusan Vlahovic was the only other player to reach double figures so scoring goals is a problem to address. Lois Openda and Randal Kolo Muani have been signed this summer to strengthen the forward line.

#1704. Inter Milan Women vs Manchester City Women - prediction, team news, lineups

By Ben Sully | 09 Nov 2026 00:29, Last updated: 09 Nov 2026 03:33

Manchester City Women will travel to Italy for Thursday's meeting with Inter Milan Women in the Women's Champions League league phase.

Inter have four points to their name after three matchdays, while Man City are a point worse off after playing out three consecutive draws.

Inter are competing in the main draw for the first time after staging an impressive fightback against two-time European champions Wolfsburg in qualifying.

After losing 2-0 to Wolfsburg in Germany, Inter recorded a 3-1 extra-time victory in the second leg before they held their nerve in the subsequent penalty shootout.

David Sassarini's side went on to take four points from their first two league phase games, edging out Hacken by a 1-0 scoreline on home turf before netting a late equaliser in a 1-1 away draw against Austria Vienna.

However, they failed to take anything from their matchday three encounter against record champions Lyon, conceding six goals without troubling the scorers in their second competitive defeat of the season.

Inter have bounced back from that 6-0 loss with consecutive 3-0 victories in domestic action, including a statement win over local rivals AC Milan on Saturday, keeping them within two points of Serie A leaders Roma.

As their focus turns to a daunting test against the Women's Super League champions, the hosts can draw inspiration from the fact they have won all of their seven competitive home games this season, keeping clean sheets in each of their last four.

While Inter are a point clear of 13th spot, Man City are sitting inside the top 12 on goal difference after starting the main draw with three consecutive draws, making them one of seven teams yet to win in the league phase this season.

The Citizens fought back from two goals down to salvage a 2-2 draw against Bayern Munich before they played out a 1-1 scoreline in their home meeting with Real Madrid.

Man City looked set to claim their first European win of the season when Bunny Shaw netted an 85th-minute penalty against Paris Saint-Germain, only for Tara Elimbi to equalise just three minutes later in a 1-1 draw.

Andree Jeglertz's side have since returned to winning ways with back-to-back Women's Super League victories against London City Lionesses and West Ham United.

Shaw netted a hat-trick in Saturday's comfortable 5-0 victory against the Hammers, sending the Citizens two points clear of Chelsea at the top of the WSL ahead of Saturday's meeting between the two title rivals.

They will be desperate to go into that crucial encounter with their unbeaten away record intact, having won three and drawn two of their five competitive away games this season.

#1703. Report: Liverpool ready to sign €100m Virgil van Dijk replacement

Virgil van Dijk has entered the final year of his current contract at Liverpool.

The Reds' captain has been a defensive colossus for almost a decade in Merseyside, but his time at Anfield could be coming to an end.

It wouldn't come as a surprise to see the Reds extend their captain, but planning has begun in case a deal can't be reached.

#1701. Opinion: Andoni Iraola's very own Ibrahima Konate has been found

Andoni Iraola's time as Liverpool manager has been a bit of a roller coaster so far.

The Spaniard took over at the start of July and, although the Reds did fairly well in their pre-season games, that same level of performance hasn't really followed them through to the actual season.

So far, the Reds have lost three games across all competitions and have failed to fill their fans with any sort of confidence that things can be turned around.

And, with the transfer window now just around the corner, fans have started to question what sort of moves Liverpool could make to improve their fortunes.

Indeed, Liverpool may have already spent around £600 million on new players over the last couple of seasons but, with the level of player they're being linked with, it feels like a lot more than that is going to be spent.

Liverpool have re-ignited their interest in Castello Lukeba

Ibrahima Konate's departure during the 2026-27 summer transfer window was one that many fans expected.

For the last couple of years, talks between the Frenchman and Liverpool about a new contract had taken place but, each time either party was asked about negotiations, nobody could give a definitive answer about whether an agreement was going to be reached.

This led fans to realise that Konate's time was up, especially when it was announced that Jeremy Jacquet would be joining Liverpool for £55 million.

From that point on, fans have come to grips with the loss of the Frenchman and have tried to source a new player to plug the gap.

That's where RB Leipzig centre-back Castello Lukeba comes in.

As per a fresh update from FootballFanCast, Liverpool are now the most likely team to sign Lukeba.

"Football FanCast sources understand that Liverpool are currently the most interested Premier League club in signing RB Leipzig centre-back Castello Lukeba," they wrote.

"The 23-year-old has attracted attention from several leading English sides, with Arsenal having monitored his development for an extended period and Manchester United also expressing interest.

"However, Liverpool are understood to have emerged as the strongest suitors, and sources understand the Frenchman's representatives have informed all three suitors of his desire to move to the Premier League."

Castello Lukeba could become Andoni Iraola's version of Ibrahima Konate

Looking back at Konate's time with Liverpool, there were definitely some highs and lows.

The Frenchman won the Premier League twice and the Champions League once but, towards the end of his time at Anfield, he was making some rather silly mistakes.

Whether he was misplacing passes or mistiming challenges, some fans were happy to see him go.

But, when he was at his best, Konate was easily one of the Premier League's best centre-backs.

This is exactly who Lukeba could become. Not only is he another French centre-back from RB Leipzig but he's also a similar age to when Konate left Leipzig for L4 back in 2021.

Much like Konate, Lukeba also has a release clause within his Leizpig contract and, although his is worth a bit more than Konate's was, it feels like 23-year-old has a lot of potential to fulfil.

Of course, these are just rumours at the moment but, of all the centre-backs linked with Liverpool ahead of the January transfer window, Lukeba is one of the deals that makes the most sense.

Manchester United boss Michael Carrick has confirmed that Harry Maguire should have enough time to recover for their clash with Liverpool after a back spasm.

The Red Devils will enter the international break in 18th place following their 4-4 draw with Aston Villa on Sunday, with the club taking just eight points from their first 10 games of the Premier League season.

To make matters worse, centre-back Maguire was replaced at half time at Old Trafford, and fears arose that he could miss the team's match against Liverpool on November 22.

However, Carrick eased those concerns and suggested that the international break could give him enough time to recover, telling MUTV: "Harry had a bad back. A really bad back spasm that he had with maybe 10, 15 minutes to go in the first half.

Ayden Heaven came on to replace Maguire, though Lisandro Martinez will also be available for United's visit to Anfield.

The game at Anfield could be defining for United for a number of reasons, but none more so than the fact a damaging defeat could be Carrick's last ever match in charge as boss.

There is a chance that he could be dismissed during the international break, though the fixture against Liverpool will still be vital considering a loss would be a worrying way for a new head coach to start their reign.

More concerning is that failure to win could leave the Red Devils last in the table after 11 matchweeks, and that would likely condemn them to a relegation battle for the remainder of the campaign.

A meeting with Liverpool will always be a significant event, but there is far more at stake than just another three points, so having as many players available for that fixture as possible will be important.

Liverpool lead the division in terms of points taken on the road this season (13), but they currently rank 18th for points taken at home (5).

The Reds have already faced Manchester City and Arsenal at Anfield, though it was demoralising for fans to see the team sink to 3-0 and 1-0 defeats in those contests.

A commanding victory against United would be Andoni Iraola's best result of the season, and it would fuel optimism in the fanbase that he could lead the Merseysiders to success.

Published: 13:29 EST, 5 November 2026 | Updated: 17:28 EST, 5 November 2026

Newcastle United star Amar Dedic was at the centre of a major police operation after he was spotted carrying a bow and arrows at a Northumberland beauty spot – with at least SIX patrol cars involved in the search for the £30million defender.

The Bosnia international sparked alarm when a concerned member of the public reported seeing him and a friend walking with the weapon near a reservoir in the countryside outside Newcastle.

Police dispatched marked and unmarked vehicles to the area in Harlow Hill, with some understood to have been armed response units, before Dedic and his companion were finally intercepted around seven miles away in the exclusive Darras Hall estate.

Sources have described the dramatic swoop on Dedic's vehicle before officers searched the car and seized a bow and arrows, with the 24-year-old questioned about his activities.

In a bizarre twist, Newcastle goalkeeper Mark Gillespie and former defender Paul Dummett arrived at the scene while police were speaking to Dedic. It is understood the pair were in the area by chance and stopped to offer assistance.

After speaking to the two men, officers were satisfied there was no threat to the public, with police subsequently stating that the equipment was believed to have been intended for recreational use.

Amar Dedic played in Newcastle's 1-0 defeat by Everton on Monday evening

Dedic was spotted with a crossbow off Military Road, the 61-mile B6318 in Northumberland

However, enquiries remain ongoing into the incident, which happened on Wednesday afternoon. It is understood that Dedic and his friend had fired some arrows while in the countryside, although it remains unclear what they were aiming at. Hunting any animal or bird with a bow and arrow or crossbow is illegal in the UK.

Dedic joined Newcastle from Benfica during the summer and has impressed at right back despite the club's difficult start to the season.

A Northumbria Police spokesperson said: 'Shortly after 1.55pm on Wednesday, we received a report of two men carrying a bow and arrows while walking along a track by the reservoir on Military Road in the Harlow Hill area.

'Officers attended and subsequently stopped a vehicle in the Darras Hall area and seized a bow and arrows. At this stage, it is understood they were for recreational use and there was no threat to the public. Enquiries are ongoing.'

#1696. ​Arteta’s ‘dynasty’ dream collides with Arsenal’s harsh reality

Mikel Arteta says he wants to create a “dynasty” at Arsenal as he threw down the gauntlet to his players to retain their Premier League title and reach a “different level”.

Arsenal are on the verge of completing a £75m deal for Brazil midfielder Bruno Guimãraes from Newcastle and have not given up hope of landing Real Madrid winger Vinícius Júnior, who has been offered an improved contract by the Spanish giants.

The Premier League champions slumped to a 3-1 defeat to Real Betis in Dublin on Wednesday night, when they paid the price for individual errors and a lethargic, sloppy defensive display.

But that did little to quell Arteta’s ambitions for the new season. “I’m even more excited [about this season], and we’re going to go and attack every possible title because that’s the ambition that we have,” he said.

“We know that we have the ability. We will go from a strength to a strength as well, whether it’s with the players that we have to take them to a different level, and with the market that is still open to recruit as well, so we are very optimistic about it.

“All the work that we’ve done – that I’ve done through the summer – is to understand what we need to do to win again and to create a dynasty in this football club. That’s the aim.”

Despite Arteta’s bullishness, he conceded Arsenal would have to be a lot better than they were against Betis. When asked about the mood in the dressing room, he said: “Very upset, given a hard time. They are fuming, but this is good. That’s what we need.”

Telegraph Sport analyses some of the talking points from a disappointing evening at the Aviva Stadium.

The importance of goalkeeper David Raya and centre-backs William Saliba and Gabriel Magalhães to Arsenal hardly needs overstating. Their title success was built on the foundations provided by that triumvirate at the back.

Raya has yet to report back from holiday after Spain’s World Cup triumph and Saliba is facing an extended spell on the sidelines with a back injury. Gabriel did appear for the second half but, watching this, Arteta is unlikely to have been dissuaded from the belief he needs another top defender to compensate for the loss of Saliba.

It may have been only Arsenal’s second game of pre-season, so a degree of legginess was understandable.

But the ease with which they were cut open and overloaded by the Spanish side, and the volume of individual errors, did not sit comfortably with Arteta with just over a fortnight until they kick off their title defence at home to newly promoted Coventry City.

Only once in 63 matches last season did Arsenal concede three goals in a single game but they were fortunate Betis did not score more. “In the first half there are two different things: to play well and to compete,” said Arteta, who saw his side trail 3-1 at the interval.

“We did the first one quite well in a lot of moments but the compete part – especially in and around our box – was not to the standards to win a football match against a good side. It’s better to give them [the goals away] in a friendly match than an official match. It’s always good when you lose a match in pre-season because it creates a bit more fire in the belly.”

Kepa Arrizabalaga will not want to watch Betis’s first goal back in a hurry. The Arsenal goalkeeper may have got a slight nudge as he came for the ball at a corner but he was all over the place and never looked even in the vaguest control of the situation. Rodrigo Riquelme scored at the far post after the ball sailed over the keeper. Arteta called it a “really sloppy goal”. With former Leeds goalkeeper Illan Meslier having arrived on a free transfer as back-up to Raya, Kepa faces an uncertain future at Arsenal. Moments like this will not help his cause.

He did not feature much last season but is probably best remembered for his torrid showing in the Carabao Cup final defeat by Manchester City in March. He looked as unconvincing here as he did then, as the former Chelsea goalkeeper also sliced a clearance in the build up to Betis’s third goal. Before then, Kai Havertz had turned over possession cheaply from which Nelson Deossa set up former West Ham midfielder Pablo Fornals to score.

Arsenal need more creativity and firepower in attack, hence the interest in Vinícius and Atlético Madrid’s Julián Alvarez. Viktor Gyokeres again looked rather limited here and the likes of Bukayo Saka and Eberechi Eze are also still to report back. Yet one of the few, brighter aspects of Arsenal’s performances was the sight of the regal looking Riccardo Calafiori marauding forward from a very nominal left-back role.

If Arsenal are going to play more adventurously this season and try to ratchet up things in the entertainment stakes then Calafiori could have a big role to play, as long as Arteta can keep him fit. He can be a potent weapon galloping forward and there were clear glimpses of that here. Harnessing that talent while not compromising too much defensive security may be one of the manager’s challenges.

Louie Copley had only been on the pitch for nine minutes – a half-time substitute for Ben White – when the 19-year-old midfielder went down largely unchallenged with what looked like a troubling knee injury. Arteta admitted afterwards that the way the teenager fell to the ground was a concern and he looked in visible pain and distress as he was treated by the medical staff before being helped off the pitch.

The fear will be of some kind of ligament damage and Arteta confirmed Copley would be scanned on Thursday. “Quite worried to be fair for the kid because the mechanism doesn’t look very positive and the symptoms that he already has,” the manager said. “So we are going to have to wait and see for tomorrow’s scan. Touch wood that is not a bad one.”

Arsenal have a corner early on in this second half as Vieira’s shot from distance deflects behind. The delivery from the left has too much on it, going over the heads of all the Arsenal players in the box, and Betis are able to clear.

Mikel Arteta has made a whole host of changes, which includes the likes of Jesus, Martinelli, Gabriel and Vieira coming on. Betis have brought the former Real Madrid man Isco on at the break.

Possession: Arsenal 63%-37% Real BetisShots: 5-7Shots on target: 2-6Corners: 1-2

Arsenal’s title triumph was built on that stout defence and conceding so few but there have been so many self-inflicted wounds here. The first and third goals came from dismal individual errors from Kepa and Havertz and the second - while a wonder strike - came after Arsenal had failed to clear their lines properly.

The first half is brought to an end and Real Betis take a 3-1 lead into the break.

Manuel Pellegrini’s side have their third goal of the night and restore their two-goal advantage. Havertz gives the ball away poorly deep inside his own half and the ball is played into Fornals. The former West Ham man has it on the edge of the box and has P Garcia in space to his right but opts to shoot. It is a clinical finish from Fornals as he picks out the bottom left corner and celebrates by crossing his arms to form irons, paying tribute to his days at West Ham.

"It's so so easy!" 🎙️The former West Ham man Pablo Fornals puts Real Betis 3-1 up against Arsenal 🌴🔨 pic.twitter.com/iyBeyS1nHd

Betis come close to restoring their two-goal advantage. Calafiori gives the ball away deep inside his own half and the ball is quickly moved onto P Garcia on the right side of the box. He opens up his body and curls a shot first time towards the far corner, forcing Kepa into the save down to his right.

Riquelme shoots from just outside the box and forces Kepa into a save down to his right.

Betis have one goal from a corner and now Arsenal do. Betis keeper Valles complains that he is being fouled by Havertz after Tzolis swung in the corner from the left and the ball comes through to Hincapie, who has the simplest of headers from inside the six-yard box.

Normal service is resumed with a Gunners goal from the corner 👏Piero Hincapié gives the @Arsenal fans reason to celebrate! 🔴 pic.twitter.com/b7h979i0Gv

Important block from P Garcia. Dowman cuts in from the right across the face of the penalty area and finds Tzolis in space to his left. Tzolis takes one touch before taking on the shot from inside the Betis box but P Garcia slides in with a crucial block.

That is quite the finish! Deossa receives the ball in a central position around 25 yards out. He takes a couple of touches before lashing a shot with his left foot. His effort flies into the top corner and Betis have a 2-0 lead. Considering the quality of the finish, I am surprised that Deossa did not celebrate more bearing in mind you do not score screamers like that every day!

Nelson Deossa...what a hit! 😱😱Real Betis double their lead over Arsenal with a stunning strike and Mikel Arteta doesn't look happy 🌴 pic.twitter.com/4J5QnjOury

Since Gyokeres misses that very good chance just a minute into the game, Arsenal have not really carved out many genuine opportunities in front of goal, other than that Tzolis wasted chance. Every time they reach the final third, they are lacking that cutting edge.

Calafiori’s role is interesting. He’s very nominally a left back but is routinely stepping into midfield and raiding forward, often ending up in positions you’d associate with a No. 10. It’s the kind of role Nico O’Reilly played under Pep Guardiola at Manchester City.

Valles is so, so lucky. The Betis keeper inexplicably passes the ball straight at Tzolis inside the Betis penalty area but Tzolis is unable to capitalise. That is a huge slice of luck for Valles as that was a ridiculous moment.

Betis have already scored one goal from a corner and they now have another corner after Nwaneri’s clearance behind. The inswinger is sent into a good area but this time Arsenal deal with the danger.

Arsenal were the better side in the early stages but Betis have grown into this and have taken confidence from that goal.

The first goal of the night goes the way of the Spaniards. The corner from the left should be dealt with by Kepa but the Arsenal keeper makes an absolute mess of it. The ball goes straight through him and comes to Riquelme at the far post. He takes one touch before firing into the net. Kepa is appealing for a free-kick but there is never a foul in there.

Real Betis strike first at the Aviva! 🌴Riquelme takes advantage of poor Arsenal defending at the corner to open the scoring 👀 pic.twitter.com/1ubVDayElP

That is dire goalkeeping from Kepa. He’s desperately tried to claim he was fouled but he just made a complete hash of it.

Betis have their first shot of the night. P Garcia receives it out on the right and cuts inside onto his left. The space opens up for him to shoot and he obliges, forcing Kepa into a save before the ball is smashed behind for a corner...

Calafiori may be on the teamsheet tonight for Arsenal at left-back but when they are in possession the Italian is moving into midfield. Lewis-Skelly, who is playing in the number six role, is dropping in between the two centre-backs when Arsenal have the ball.

Betis win a free-kick out on the left, with the chance to send it into the Arsenal penalty area for the first time tonight. It is clipped into a good area but Kepa is out of his goal to catch it.

Arsenal should be ahead one minute into the game with their first attack of the game. Havertz picks up the ball on the corner of the box out on the left and passes it inside to Gyokeres. The Swedish striker takes one touch before shooting from the edge of the six-yard box but his shot is saved. In reality, Gyokeres should not have given Valles in the Betis goal any chance of saving that one.

Both sides emerge from the tunnel, Arsenal led out by Ben White and Betis by former Arsenal man Hector Bellerin, and make their way past the Premier League trophy. We are moments away from kick-off in Dublin.

Arsenal: Kepa; White, Mosquera, Hincapie, Calafiori; Lewis-Skelly, Havertz, Nwaneri; Dowman, Gyokeres, Tzolis.

Real Betis: Valles, Bellerin, Bartra, Natan, F.Garcia; Bernal, Gnangoro, Fornals; P.Garcia, Riquelme, Deossa.

“When I see the training and how hungry they are for every training drill, that means everybody is ready to compete at the highest level. When you are a player of Arsenal, you compete for every title that is possible. It is not only about the Premier League, it is about all the competitions we are playing for. I see a clear mindset and everything, that everybody is on the same page to win titles here. I saw it from the first training and I think when you train like that in the game, it makes it even better. I came here ready, with my fitness level and I was happy that I could show it here as well. I want to be myself and to show on the pitch all the passion and desire to win because I really like to win games and to give everything.

“If I give 100% for every game and every duel, I think who does not like this? I think that is the best thing for a football player, and then you will always have the support from the supporters. I am thinking about how to improve and settle as fast as possible in the club, because I have the opportunity to train directly with the team from the beginning of the season, to play pre-season games and then to go to official games. This is a chance to play directly from the beginning and then it is up to me to show the qualities and what I can bring to the team. I am pretty confident I will show it in the next games.”

Premier League champions Arsenal continue their preparations for the new season as they take on Spanish side Real Betis at the Aviva Stadium in Dublin, with this being the first-ever meeting between the two sides. This is the first time Arsenal have played a pre-season game in Dublin since August 2018, when they drew 1-1 with London rivals Chelsea, with Arsenal winning on penalties.

Arsenal beat Girona 4-1 in their opening game of pre-season, with new signing Christos Tzolis on the scoresheet in his first appearance for the club. After today, Arsenal have three more games, including the Community Shield, before they kick off the defence of their Premier League crown at home against newly-promoted Coventry on opening night of the new season. They are closing in on a deal for Newcastle captain Bruno Guimaraes, who is set to become one of Arsenal’s most expensive signings. Mikel Arteta’s side have been dealt a blow ahead of the season with the news that France centre-back William Saliba will miss an extended period due to a back injury. The likes of Declan Rice, Bukayo Saka and Noni Madueke are still yet to return after their World Cup exploits.

Real Betis, under the management of former Manchester City boss Manuel Pellegrini, finished fifth in La Liga last season and have therefore qualified for this coming season’s Champions League after a 20-year absence from the competition. Pellegrini has led Betis into European competitions for five consecutive seasons, which includes losing the 2025 Europa Conference League final to Chelsea. They have been busy in pre-season action already having played five games up to this point. They have won four of the five, including a 4-0 victory over Lyon, with just one defeat coming against Granada.

They have a number of former Premier League players in their ranks, including Antony, Giovani Lo Celso, Pablo Fornals and former Arsenal man Hector Bellerin. Real Betis have already played a number of friendlies as they build up to the start of their season, which begins on August 21 when they take on Real Sociedad.

#1694. Liverpool injury news: Dominik Szoboszlai latest as 'knee' timeline assessed before Man United Premier League game at Anfield

By Lewis Nolan | 09 Nov 2026 02:23, Last updated: 09 Nov 2026 02:25

Dominik Szoboszlai has suffered a knee injury and is a doubt for the international break and the games after, Liverpool boss Andoni Iraola has revealed.

The midfielder was part of the Reds team that came away from Selhurst Park with three points on Sunday, helping the Merseysiders win 3-1 against Crystal Palace.

However, Szoboszlai appeared to be struggling close to half time with a knee issue, and while he played in the second half, he was substituted in the 69th minute for Trey Nyoni.

Speaking to reporters, Iraola was not sure if Szoboszlai would play any games for Hungary over the international break, saying: "Yes, [Dominik] has, I don't know [if it's] a problem, but he definitely wasn't 100%. Let's see. The last thing we need now is to lose players in the international games.

"Last time, in the international break, we lost three very important players, so now I'm praying. It's the last thing we need. I think he extended a little bit the knee, it was fine, but not 100%, so he has to be careful to see if he can play with the national team or not.

"We will see, and also hope that it doesn't happen like the other break where we lost [Isak], Cody [Gakpo] and Dom. So, touch wood we are in a better place in two weeks."

Szoboszlai has already suffered a hamstring injury, and with Liverpool set to play Manchester United on November 22, Iraola will want the 26-year-old to rest over the next two weeks.

Knee injuries can be complex and involve lengthy periods on the sidelines, but it seems likely that Szoboszlai has avoided the worst possible outcome.

A Grade 1 problem could be a mild sprain, though that would still put the Hungarian's participation in the United game at risk given it would require anywhere from one to three weeks on the treatment table.

It would also make the 26-year-old a doubt for the club's Champions League clash with Club Brugge on November 25, though he would almost certainly be back for the Merseyside derby on November 29.

A Grade 2 injury would involve three to six weeks away from the pitch, and that could leave Szoboszlai unavailable until around Christmas.

Nyoni came on for Szoboszlai against Palace, and the 19-year-old performed excellently, winning two of his three duels and making four defensive contributions, while also playing a significant role in Alexander Isak's goal.

There is an argument that the teenager should be in the starting XI regardless of Szoboszlai's fitness, especially as he has shown he is far more comfortable with the ball in a double pivot.

The youngster was excellent against Arsenal on November 1, and if Nyoni was to play well against United at Anfield, Iraola would find it hard to drop him.

#1692. Chelsea in the race? Nico Paz sets the 2027 transfer market alight, but who can actually afford him?

By Axel Clody | 09 Nov 2026 07:02, Last updated: 09 Nov 2026 07:03

Among the best-performing players in Europe since the start of the season, Nico Paz is the dream of many of the continent’s heavyweights. But a three-figure sum in millions (more than £85m / €100m) will undoubtedly be needed to sign the Argentina international.

Nico Paz was the star of the show as Como thrashed RC Lens 9-1 in the Champions League on Wednesday. A key figure for the Italian side for three seasons, the Argentine number 10 lit up the game with his talent, scoring one goal and providing two assists. In his last five outings, the 22-year-old has even accumulated five goals and five assists.

Unsurprisingly, the best clubs on the planet are battling to secure his services and one of them has a competitive advantage: Real Madrid. Real Madrid hold a buy-back clause of £68m (€80m), included when he was sold to Como in 2024 for £56.1m (€66m). It cannot, however, be activated before next summer.

Real Madrid are therefore the favourites to bring back their former player at such a price, while other European giants will probably find it harder to compete.

It is easy to imagine that Como will not sell their star cheaply and will ask for at least £85m (€100m) to let Nico Paz go to another club. That sum seems too high for Barcelona, who have not spent such an amount since 2019, when they signed Antoine Griezmann.

Because of the sanctions that still threaten the club, Manchester City also appear to be out of the running for now. Their rivals Manchester United, meanwhile, have clearly lost some of their lustre and would probably be less attractive in the eyes of the Argentine.

A transfer to Paris Saint-Germain cannot be ruled out, given that the double reigning European champions have the means to pull out such a big sum. Furthermore, the playing philosophy put in place by Luis Enrique would probably appeal to the Argentina star.

The Premier League also remains an avenue to consider. While Liverpool have Florian Wirtz in this role, Chelsea, for their part, are not afraid of stacking up talents (and expensive transfers) and, despite the presence of Cole Palmer, it would not be so surprising to see Chelsea join the race.

For now, Real Madrid appear to be in pole position to sign him in the summer of 2027, but this saga could heat up in the coming months if Nico Paz continues to perform this well.

#1690. Genoa 1-2 AC Milan: Cisse and Pulisic score in hard-fought victory

AC Milan secured a much-needed three points on Sunday afternoon as they beat an in-form Genoa side 2-1 at the Stadio Luigi Ferraris.

The groundwork for the victory was laid in the first half, when Alphadjo Cisse slotted in a cut-back from Adrien Rabiot to get his eighth of the campaign, before Christian Pulisic buried a square pass from Gonçalo Ramos after a stray pass inside the box.

Read SempreMilan ad-free and get access to exclusive news. Click here for a free trial!

Ellertsson made it a very nervy finish for the Rossoneri with a goal inside the final few minutes from a long-range strike, but Milan did ultimately manage to hang on for what was an important three points.

It means that a top four spot has been reclaimed for the time being while waiting to see how the game between Inter and Como plays out, and it eases some of the pressure heading into the international break.

Ruben Amorim chose to make five changes from Thursday’s defeat to Ferencvaros. Mike Maignan, Mario Gila, Luka Modric, Diego Moreira and Christian Pulisic all came into the side, though there were some question marks about whether it would be a four or three-man defence based on the names selected.

Genoa started on the front foot and they immediately created an opening inside the first minute. Koni De Winter allowed Osmajic to run off his shoulder and get a shot off from the left side of the box, but Maignan watched it roll narrowly wide of the far post.

One minute after Vitinha had back-heeled a near-post cross into Maignan’s hands, Milan created their first opening. Pulisic’s cross from the byline wasn’t well-aimed but the clearance fell straight to Ramos, who didn’t quite connect right with his effort and sent it a couple of yards wide of the far post.

Milan continued to knock on the door and Ramos almost found himself on the end of a golden opportunity when Gila was found on the overlap and provided a cut-back, though Marcandalli did brilliantly to cut out the danger.

Then, in the 13th minute, Milan did take the lead through Alphadjo Cisse. The goal was assisted by Adrien Rabiot who found the run of the Italian with a nice square ball, but Pulisic was the one who won possession back on the high press to create the opportunity, which was well finished by Cisse for his eighth goal of the campaign.

In the 19th minute, the Rossoneri doubled their lead. Another successful press forced Ostigard into a mistake as his square ball back towards the goalkeeper was cut off by Ramos. The Portuguese squared to Pulisic after evading a defender, and the American made no mistake as he fired inside the near post to make it 2-0.

Right on the half-hour mark, Genoa thought they had got themselves back into the game when Osmajic headed past Maignan having escaped his man to be found by Vitinha’s flick-on. However, the offside flag was raised and the decision was upheld, though it looked very close.

Despite being two goals up, Milan never gave the impression of being in control and Genoa had a couple of half-chances towards the end of the half, including an Ostigard header that Maignan managed to claim.

The start to the second half was certainly a fractious one, and the Milan players were surrounding the referee Davide Massa five minutes into it when Rabiot seized on a loose touch from Marcandalli to run in behind.

He was dragged back by the defender who appeared to be the last man, but a yellow card was deemed to be sufficient. Rabiot got a yellow too for his protests, and three members of the Milan coaching staff were shown a red.

Amorim opted to make a couple of changes on the hour mark, with Cisse making way for Omari Hutchinson and Diawara coming off for Filippo Terracciano.

As the game entered the final 20 minutes, Milan began to look comfortable with their lead but at times complacent too. Musah gave possession away in the left-back position and it gave Vitinha a dangerous position to get a shot off, though Maignan did well to parry it away.

The pressure continued to come from the Rossoblu, and El Shaarawy had a chance off the bench when a cross found him in the box. He brought it down well, but Terracciano got a knee to it to deflect it over. Pulisic made way for Ardon Jashari after.

Inside the final few minutes Pervis Estupinan became the last player to come, replacing Musah. The sub was made just before El Shaarawy lined up a free-kick from about 22 yards out, and it would yield Genoa’s route back into the game.

The initial shot was blocked as it went into a crowd but was not cleared, allowing Ellertsson all the time in the world to step up and strike one from distance that nestled inside the right post with Maignan rooted. Game on with two minutes of normal time left.
